title: POC Weekly Sync - Onboarding & Environment Readiness
summary: Weekly POC sync to review initial benchmark results on latency/cost, confirm VPC/KMS access for Private deployment, discuss tuning (batching/quant), and agree next steps for a production-like benchmark next week.
topics: initial perf results and tuning suggestions
action_items: Maya Patel - Send security package (SOC2 summary, encryption details) and SSO docs - due 2026-07-10
Carlos Ruiz - Prepare a short runbook for KV cache warmup and batching config used in last run - due 2026-07-09
Marcus Lee - Confirm VPC peering CIDR and open port checklist (22, 443, custom infra ports) and share VPN details - due 2026-07-09
Alyssa Chen - Share sample prompt set and expected latency SLOs for production traffic - due 2026-07-10
next_steps: Redwood to run a production-like benchmark on the dedicated pilot cluster next Tue (2026-07-14)
Customer to complete KMS key grant and SSO setup by next Friday
Schedule a security deep-dive with Ben and Redwood security next week (30-45m)
transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-07-08 Time: 11:00 AM PDT Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Dana Liu (Redwood CSM), Alyssa Chen (LumenHealth ML), Marcus Lee (LumenHealth Infra), Priya N. (CTO), Ben Ortiz (Security)
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick check in, I'll kick us off. Agenda: review the run from last week, check access status for the private env, and make sure we're set for the next benchmark.
[00:22] Alyssa: Yep thanks Maya, we ran the test suite against the pilot cluster wednesday, saw decent throughput but some tail latency spikes, i'll share the logs after.
[00:35] Carlos: Cool can you share the exact job config? batch sizes, seq lengths, token limits? That helps map to batching behavior.
[00:48] Alyssa: Sure, it was mostly 512 token sequences, batch size 8, we had typical prompt mix (few-shot + instruction). On average p95 was ~480ms but occasionally hit 1.2s on tails.
[01:10] Carlos: Okay that matches what we saw in the telemetry — most tokens at ~420-500ms, spikes when model cache misses and KV cache warmup happened. We suspect prefix/kvcache cold starts for rare long-context prompts.
[01:38] Marcus: Quick infra note: we were using a small NAT gateway for egress and the network path added about ~30-40ms. We can move to a peered route to reduce that.
[01:54] Maya: Good call. On the security/access side Marcus, last check from our side you were going to set up the KMS grant and the SAML/SSO. Where are we?
[02:10] Marcus: We're mostly done with SSO. Ben will handle the KMS policy — we have an internal process to approve external key grants, should be finished by end of week.
[02:28] Ben: I reviewed the initial security pack, couple questions on key rotation and audit log retention - how does Redwood surface the audit logs for private? Are they pushed to our CloudWatch or stored locally?
[02:43] Dana: For Private deployment we support pushing audit events to your CloudWatch/Splunk, and we also keep replayable audit logs in the control plane for 90 days. I'll send the exact retention table.
[03:05] Ben: Ok please add that in the security doc, and also any HSM/KMS integration notes.
[03:16] Alyssa: Back on perf — Carlos, you mentioned batching config; do you recommend increasing batch size? We're worried about p95 vs cost tradeoff.
[03:28] Carlos: Right so there's a few levers: increase batching up to what your latency SLO allows, enable prefix caching for repetitive prompts, and consider a quantized model variant for lower-cost inference. For this workload, bumping batch to 12 gave ~15% cost drop with small median latency increase but tail risk went up.
[03:54] Priya: Curious on quantization — do you have baseline quality regressions for our LLM prompts? We can't sacrifice accuracy for cost.
[04:06] Carlos: We ran evals on your prompt set with int8 and q4 variants; top-line: int8 had negligible regression on classification tasks but some hallucination uptick on the long instruction chains. We can run an on-your-data eval and surface metrics.
[04:30] Alyssa: Please do that — we'll need a comparison CSV with exact prompts so we can sign off.
[04:38] Maya: We'll include that in the security+eval package. Also, small FYI — we noticed your token distribution skewed heavier on a few prefix classes, so caching will be very helpful.
[04:55] Marcus: On environment readiness, I wanted to confirm the network ports and peering. We're planning VPC peering into the Redwood private subnet, can you confirm the required CIDR ranges and SG rules?
[05:12] Carlos: We'll need outbound 443 to Redwood control plane IPs for telemetry, and inbound from our dedicated infra for health checks. For the private model hosting nodes, peering CIDR should not overlap — we'll share recommended ranges.
[05:28] Maya: I'll put a checklist in the follow-up email.
[05:36] Alyssa: One weird thing: during the run we saw some tokenization mismatches where model token count was higher than expected, doubled for emojis and some unicode. Did you see that in the logs?
[05:50] Carlos: Yeah there were a few outliers — our tokenizer variant differs slightly; we can align tokenizers or canonicalize input at the edge. That's an easy fix.
[06:05] Priya: Timeline question — if we finish KMS+SSO and the benchmark next week goes well, what's the earliest we can scale to 3x production?
[06:20] Maya: For Redwood Dedicated pilot, after a successful benchmark and security sign-off, we can schedule reserved capacity rollout in about 4-6 weeks depending on GPU availability and your contract terms. But we can enable burst capacity earlier for load spikes.
[06:38] Marcus: Good to know. Back to results: Alyssa, do you have the cost per 1k tokens numbers?
[06:45] Alyssa: Preliminary: about $1.8 per 1k tokens at current config on the pilot cluster. We're hoping to bring that down to under $1.0 with batching + quantization.
[06:58] Carlos: That aligns; with q4 and batching and prefix cache, we typically see 35-50% token-cost reduction depending on hit rate.
[07:12] Ben: Security question — encryption in transit and at rest, are we managing keys or is Redwood?
[07:20] Maya: For Private, you manage KMS keys; Redwood integrates with your KMS and never stores plaintext model inputs. We can provide flow diagrams.
[07:30] Ben: Ok please share diagrams and the HSM notes.
[07:36] Dana: Also we'll include RBAC roles and recommended SAML groups mapping.
[07:45] Alyssa: About the benchmark next Tue — do you need a specific dataset or can we point you at our traffic replay logs?
[07:56] Carlos: Traffic replay logs are ideal; if you can provide a 10k-100k request sample with timing distribution that helps simulate production. If not, we'll bootstrap with your sample prompt set and synthetic timing.
[08:12] Alyssa: I'll extract a sample set and share.
[08:20] Priya: Any blockers on our side besides KMS?
[08:25] Marcus: We're just waiting on the external key grant approval and I'll finalize peering details.
[08:32] Maya: Great. Quick walkthrough of the telemetry screenshots we uploaded — (link shared) — p90/p95 charts show the spikes correlate with cache misses and GC cycles on the model host, we suggested tuning the GC interval and increasing cache RAM in the node config.
[08:51] Carlos: Also worth noting, for long sequences the KV cache memory growth was higher than expected — increasing kvcache shard sizes across the pool smoothed the spikes.
[09:04] Alyssa: Is there an easy knob to auto-scale the kv cache?
[09:08] Carlos: Not automatic yet; autoscaling is at the node level, but we have heuristics to rebalance kv shards during low load. We'll include those suggested configs.
[09:22] Ben: On compliance — do you have a standard SOC2 addendum for private deployments?
[09:27] Dana: Yes, we'll attach the SOC2 summary and addendum that outlines responsibilities.
[09:32] Maya: Ok let's move to concrete next steps — Carlos will run the production-like benchmark on the dedicated pilot cluster next Tue; Marcus will finish KMS grant and share peering details; Alyssa will provide sample traffic and prompt set. Redwood will send security + eval package.
[09:55] Marcus: One last note: for our legal procurement timeline, we need pricing and a basic SOW to start internal approvals — can you send indicative pricing?
[10:05] Maya: Absolutely, I'll send a pilot pricing sheet and an indicative SOW by EOD tomorrow.
[10:12] Priya: If benchmark results are good, we'll loop procurement and aim to finalize pilot contract in 3 weeks.
[10:20] Maya: Great. Any other questions?
[10:24] Alyssa: No, thanks everyone.
[10:26] Ben: All good.
[10:30] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the items and email.
[45:00] End of meeting.
